analysis:
The changes add a selected-model recovery mechanism (selectedModelRecovery, noteSelectedModelUnloaded, savedEnabledModels), and the units wire it into the existing fences.

- AddonHold.swift:204-207 (head): enterAddonHold now also cancels selectedModelRecovery.attempt. This strengthens the T-059/TB-012 model-load fence, so a recovery load does not race the unload. Loads that slip through are still refused by addonHoldLoadRefusal (line 342).
- AutopilotBusy.swift:22 (head): the .preload busy reason now covers an in-flight recovery attempt. This makes autopilot rejection more conservative and widens no admission.
- Autopilot.swift:213 (head): after each victim unload succeeds, noteSelectedModelUnloaded(victim, by: command) is called. Its implementation is not supplied. I assume it records an intentional coordinator-directed unload so recovery does not reload the evicted model.
- AutopilotControl.swift:76 (head): refreshAutopilotSettings now caches savedEnabledModels from the operator-owned config file before the download and consent checks. The file is operator-controlled under TB-003, so this is not a new trust escalation. It does not touch consent, revision or lease logic.

None of these changes touch encryption, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011/T-053) or the prefix cache (T-041).

Questions for integration (the implementations are not in these units):
- Does selectedModelRecovery's reload path consult addonHoldLoadRefusal, checkAutopilotLoadOwnership and servingDrain/isShuttingDown, and respect autopilotAllowsModel? Otherwise recovery could load models during a hold, autopilot command or drain (T-059, A-018 availability).
- Is the recovery attempt bounded, with backoff? Repeated reloads could cause a load/unload loop or GPU monopolization (T-029-like DoS).
- Does savedEnabledModels widen which models may be served beyond what the coordinator advertises or validates? Model identity is still gated by coordinator weight-hash policy (T-012/T-027).
- Is the recovery attempt cleared when the hold ends, so busy reporting does not stick?

No concrete regression was found in the supplied lines.
